claims.text: Hydrocortisone 15–25 mg/day total in 2–3 divided doses,
claims.quote: hydrocortisone (identical to cortisol) is given in 2 or 3 divided doses with a typical total daily dose of 15 to 25 mg

claims.text: eg, 10 mg, 5 mg, 5 mg (half in the morning);
claims.quote: One regimen gives half the total in the morning, and the remaining half split between lunchtime and early evening (eg, 10 mg, 5 mg, 5 mg).
Doses immediately before bed should generally be avoided because they may cause insomnia.

claims.text: Alternative: prednisolone 4–5 mg PO in the morning.
claims.quote: Alternatively, prednisolone 4 to 5 mg orally in the morning

claims.text: With coexisting DM, hydrocortisone usually ≤ 30 mg/day; higher doses increase insulin requirements.
claims.quote: In patients with coexisting diabetes mellitus and Addison disease, the hydrocortisone dose usually should not be > 30 mg/day. Higher doses of hydrocortisone increase insulin requirements.

claims.text: Teach self-injection of parenteral hydrocortisone for emergencies
claims.quote: taught to self-administer parenteral hydrocortisone for urgent situations
A preloaded syringe with 100 mg hydrocortisone should be available to the patient for intramuscular or subcutaneous administration.

claims.text: carry ID with the diagnosis and glucocorticoid dose.
claims.quote: Identification giving the diagnosis and glucocorticoid dose may help in case of adrenal crisis that renders the patient unable to communicate.

claims.text: CYP3A4 inducers (phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampin, barbiturates) may require a higher steroid dose; inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, erythromycin) raise levels.
claims.quote: Drugs which induce cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP 3A4) enzyme activity (e.g., barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampin ) may enhance the metabolism of corticosteroids and require that the dosage of the corticosteroid be increased. Drugs which inhibit CYP 3A4 (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, indinavir, macrolide antibiotics such as erythromycin ) have the potential to result in increased plasma concentrations of corticosteroids.
claims.locator: Precautions › Drug Interactions › Hepatic Enzyme Inducers, Inhibitors and Substrates

claims.quote: Concomitant use of aspirin (or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents ) and corticosteroids increases the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

claims.text: Warfarin: response usually inhibited; monitor INR often.
claims.quote: Co-administration of corticosteroids and warfarin usually results in inhibition of response to warfarin, although there have been some conflicting reports. Therefore, coagulation indices should be monitored frequently to maintain the desired anticoagulant effect.
When corticosteroids are administered concomitantly with potassium-depleting agents (e.g., amphotericin B, diuretics ), patients should be observed closely for development of hypokalemia.
